title: The Supreme Court Just Told India's Exam Agency to Learn From the One Body That Has Never Had a Paper Leak.
excerpt: NEET UG 2026 was cancelled after a widespread paper leak. 23 lakh students must retake it on June 21. The court wants the NTA to explain how this keeps happening.
body:
The Supreme Court of India has delivered its sharpest rebuke yet of the National Testing Agency, telling the exam body to learn from institutions that have never suffered a paper leak — and singling out the UPSC as the gold standard it has failed to match.

"UPSC has never been in a situation like this. You need to learn," Justice P.S. Narasimha said during a hearing on petitions arising from the cancellation of the NEET-UG 2026 examination, which was scrapped after a widespread paper leak was detected in the May 3 test.

## 23 Lakh Students in Limbo

The cancellation has thrown the medical admission cycle into chaos. More than 23 lakh students who sat for the exam now face a re-test scheduled for June 21 — barely seven weeks after the original test date and in the middle of a brutal summer heatwave across northern India.

The bench, comprising Justices Narasimha and Alok Aradhe, did not mince words about the structural failures that allowed the leak to happen.

"The real problem won't stop till actual accountability arises. Not in terms of so-and-so will be liable — it will be effective when we know which individual shoulders the responsibility," Justice Narasimha observed. "The problem is that most institutions are ad hoc. It's a phenomenon that is everywhere in the country."

## NTA Claims Reforms, Court Wants Proof

The NTA filed an affidavit claiming it has implemented "wide-ranging security reforms" since the leak was discovered. These include enhanced paper transportation protocols, encrypted digital systems, and stricter identity verification at exam centres.

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta told the court that Prime Minister Narendra Modi is "personally supervising the situation" to ensure no further lapses occur.

But the court was unconvinced by assurances alone. It directed the Union of India to file a detailed affidavit outlining how an "institutional memory of continuity" could be built within the NTA through specialised, permanent staff — rather than the ad hoc appointments that have characterised the agency since its creation.

## CBT Petition Deferred

A separate petition sought an emergency order to conduct the June 21 re-exam in Computer-Based Test (CBT) mode instead of the existing pen-and-paper format. The court declined, noting the immense logistical pressure the NTA already faces.

"They are reholding the exam. The kind of pressure they have — we will keep it after vacation," Justice Narasimha said, deferring the matter to July.

The NTA itself has signalled a long-term shift, telling the court that it plans to transition NEET-UG to a fully computer-based format starting with the next examination cycle, in consultation with the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.

## A Pattern of Failure

This is the second consecutive year that NEET-UG has been embroiled in controversy. The 2024 examination faced allegations of irregularities in scoring and paper distribution, prompting the Supreme Court to appoint a committee led by Dr. K. Radhakrishnan to recommend reforms. Many of those recommendations, the petitioners argue, were never meaningfully implemented.

The Federation of All India Medical Association and the United Doctors Front have called for the NTA to be dissolved entirely and replaced with an independent statutory body equipped with proper technological safeguards and institutional accountability.

## What It Means for NRI Families

For Indian diaspora families whose children aspire to study medicine in India — or who have relatives preparing for the exam — the crisis underscores a deeper systemic problem. India's most important entrance examinations remain vulnerable to organised cheating networks that exploit physical logistics chains, strong rooms, and transportation systems.

The June 21 re-test will be watched closely, not just for whether it proceeds without incident, but for whether the reforms the NTA claims to have made actually hold under pressure. The Supreme Court has listed the matter for further hearing in the second week of July, after the exam is over and the data is in.

*The NEET UG 2026 re-exam is scheduled for June 21 at centres across India. Results from the cancelled May 3 test have been voided.*
author: Diaspora Desk
